title: Fruit and the mind
literal_meaning: Fruit grows according to the mind.
explanation: The entry explains the opening as according to one’s mental state or thought. Fruit supplies an image of an outcome. Our reading asks how an attitude shapes the way someone approaches work; it does not claim that thoughts alone control events. Neither success nor suffering can be diagnosed from this short line.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ନିଜ ମନ ବା ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନୁସାରେ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଫଳ ଏଠି ପରିଣାମର ଛବି ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ କାମକୁ କିପରି ଆଗେଇ ନିଏ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି; କେବଳ ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ଘଟଣା ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନାହିଁ। ଏତିକି କଥାରୁ କାହାର ସଫଳତା ବା କଷ୍ଟର କାରଣ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading links outlook with approach, without promising control over results.
odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ ଓ କାମର ଧାରାର ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ଫଳ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରର କାମ ଆରମ୍ଭ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏଥିରେ କିଛି ହେବନି।” ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଫଳ କଣ ହେବ ଜାଣିନି; କିନ୍ତୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାଟି ମନ ଦେଇ କରିବା।” / Before a reading-group project begins, someone dismisses it. A friend recalls the saying: “I cannot promise the outcome, but let us make a thoughtful attempt.” This exchange is invented.
cultural_context: The following Jagannath Bhagabata verse is a separate literary illustration, not evidence that Jagannath authored this saying. No psychological law, guaranteed reward or blame for hardship is inferred.
